chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Al-Ḥakam, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “My father gave me a house in charity, then it occurred to him to take it back, while our judges rule for me regarding it.”

So he said: “Excellent is what your judges ruled by, and evil is what your father did. Charity is only for Allah, Mighty and Majestic; so whatever is made for Allah, there is no return in it for him. If you dispute with him, then do not raise your voice over him, and if he raises his voice, then lower your voice.”
He said: I said to him, “He has indeed passed away.” He said: “Then be at ease with it.”

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: charity given for the sake of Allah
key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ: gave in charity as an act of ṣadaqah
key_terms.خَاصَمْتَهُ: you disputed or litigated with him
key_terms.رَجْعَةَ: taking back or reclaiming what was given
key_terms.صَوْتَكَ: your voice, referring to etiquette in speech
key_terms.فَأَطِبْ: be at ease and content with it
key_terms.قُضَاتُنَا: our judges who issued a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Can a father take back a house he gave in charity to his son?
ai.summary: This hadith states that property given as ṣadaqah for Allah cannot be reclaimed by the donor. It also teaches proper conduct toward one's father during dispute, instructing the son not to raise his voice even when the father does. After the father's death, the Imam عليه السلام assures him that he may keep the house with a clear conscience.
